question: What makes a nutrient 'essential'?

options.A: It is only found in expensive dietary supplements.
options.B: The body cannot make it, so it must come from food.
options.C: The body produces it in massive quantities daily.
options.D: It provides zero calories but tastes sweet.

explanation: If our bodies can't manufacture it on their own, it's 'essential' that we eat it. Simple as that!

question: How do lipid-soluble (steroid) hormones usually work inside a cell?

options.A: By using second messengers on the outside of the cell membrane
options.B: By blocking enzyme actions directly in the extracellular fluid
options.C: By binding to internal receptors and altering gene expression
options.D: By destroying the cell membrane to release stored energy

explanation: Because they love fats, steroid hormones slide right through the cell membrane, head inside, and talk directly to the cell's DNA to make new proteins.

question: When is chemical disinfection most commonly used in a healthcare facility?

options.A: For treating liquid infectious waste and laboratory cultures
options.B: For packaging expired patient food trays
options.C: For disposing of heavy metal surgical instruments
options.D: For processing large wooden crates and office furniture

explanation: Liquid waste and lab cultures are often treated directly with chemical disinfectants to make them safe before they go down the sewer lines.

question: Which healthcare professional helps a patient with severe swallowing difficulties eat safely?

options.A: Speech pathologist
options.B: Biomedical engineer
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Radiologic technologist

explanation: Don't let the title fool you—speech therapists are experts in mouth muscles, chewing, and safe swallowing (dysphagia) too!

question: What is the most important daily protection for a leprosy patient whose feet have lost feeling?

options.A: Soaking the feet in hot water daily to stimulate blood flow
options.B: Applying strong chemical antiseptics to unbroken skin daily
options.C: Wearing well-fitted, protective footwear at all times
options.D: Binding the toes tightly together to prevent accidental stubbing

explanation: Spot on! Since they can't feel pain, good shoes protect their soles from everyday cuts, stones, and ulcers.

question: Why is food safety especially critical for patients with weakened immune systems?

options.A: Their bodies struggle to fight off foodborne infections
options.B: Bad water changes their skin color
options.C: Dirty food automatically stops medicines from working
options.D: Uncooked meat increases muscle mass too fast

explanation: Spot on! An immune system that is down cannot easily fight off germs from bad food, leading to serious illness.

question: A ward records 50 patients with hypertension out of 200 patients screened. What percentage is that?

options.A: 20 percent
options.B: 10 percent
options.C: 25 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Brilliant! 50 divided by 200 gives you 0.25, which translates nicely to 25 percent.

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance in community nursing?

options.A: To collect health data for ongoing analysis and planning
options.B: To manufacture vaccines for local primary health centers
options.C: To provide individual bedside nursing care in hospitals
options.D: To punish communities that fail to meet health targets

explanation: Think of surveillance as keeping a close eye on community health trends. By gathering data continually, nurses and health planners can spot issues early and plan the right actions to keep everyone safe and well!

question: What is the very first thing you must do if a patient shows signs of an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Stop the medication immediately
options.B: Wait forty minutes to see if it passes
options.C: Give a double dose of antihistamines
options.D: Increase the intravenous fluid rate

explanation: Safety first! Always stop the trigger drug right away to keep things from getting worse. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: As a nursing student, why is it helpful to know different research categories?

options.A: To write prescriptions for patients independently
options.B: To diagnose complex diseases without a doctor
options.C: To replace hands-on clinical ward practice
options.D: To decide if a study can guide safe patient care

explanation: Spot on! Knowing research categories helps you evaluate evidence so you can confidently apply safe, proven ideas when caring for your patients. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h1)

question: What does population health nursing primarily focus on?

options.A: The financial balance sheet of a health clinic
options.B: The health outcomes of an entire group of people
options.C: The surgical procedures performed in a single hospital ward
options.D: The genetic profile of an individual patient

explanation: Population health looks beyond the individual patient to protect and promote the well-being of whole communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the main reason the brain undergoes structural changes during pregnancy?

options.A: To prepare the mother for caregiving and protect the baby
options.B: To slow down metabolic rates and prevent physical exhaustion
options.C: To permanently reduce the overall cognitive capacity of the woman
options.D: To compensate for a temporary lack of oxygen in the brain

explanation: It's fascinating how nature works! These brain changes help fine-tune maternal behavior and build emotional strength for looking after the little one.

question: Why is it smart to talk with local leaders and traditional healers during a community assessment?

options.A: They make all final decisions regarding hospital medication stock
options.B: They possess vital insights into hidden health burdens and local practices
options.C: They are legally required to sign off on all nursing licenses
options.D: They manage the financial budgets of government hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Local leaders and traditional healers know the community inside out. They see things and know practices that official reports often miss.

question: A village has no clinic, and residents must travel hours on bad roads just to get basic vaccines. What is the best way to solve this spatial barrier?

options.A: Outreach mobile health clinics visiting the community regularly
options.B: Closing all remaining health posts and telling patients to move to the city
options.C: Waiting for the community to build a multi-story teaching hospital
options.D: Punishing residents for failing to travel to town for healthcare

explanation: Brilliant! Mobile clinics bring care directly to the people, bypassing the challenge of bad roads and long distances.

question: What is one of the most important daily fluid instructions to give a patient managing gout?

options.A: Drink plenty of water daily
options.B: Only drink liquids during mealtimes
options.C: Avoid water and drink soda instead
options.D: Restrict all fluids to prevent swelling

explanation: Correct! Drinking lots of water helps the kidneys flush out extra uric acid before it has a chance to form stubborn crystals.

question: What is a key role for the nurse when caring for a patient dealing with sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Coordinating referrals and ensuring the patient transitions smoothly between specialists
options.B: Deciding which prescription drugs the pharmacy will stock
options.C: Diagnosing rare endocrine disorders without physician oversight
options.D: Performing advanced surgical procedures independently in the clinic

explanation: Nurses act as the bridge! We connect patients with the right specialists (like therapists or urologists) to make sure they get team-based, compassionate care.

question: If a patient is stable and suddenly starts getting worse during an ABCDEF check, what should the team do right away?

options.A: Rush the patient to the operating theatre
options.B: Go straight back to step A and check the airway again
options.C: Finish the rest of the protocol steps first
options.D: Wait at the bedside for the doctor to arrive

explanation: Spot on! If a patient takes a turn for the worse, always cycle right back to the beginning (Airway) to catch any new breathing or airway trouble. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: What is the main goal of sperm capacitation inside the female reproductive tract?

options.A: To prepare the sperm membrane and make it capable of fertilizing the oocyte
options.B: To slow down sperm movement so they rest before reaching the egg
options.C: To increase the total volume of seminal fluid for easier transport
options.D: To attach extra chromosomes to the sperm tail for genetic diversity

explanation: Capacitation is like a final readiness training. It changes the sperm's membrane so it gains the strength to pierce the egg's outer layers.

question: What is the main goal of actively managing the third stage of labor for an anaemic patient?

options.A: To force the placenta out before contractions begin
options.B: To speed up cervix opening in early labor
options.C: To reduce blood loss and stop dangerous postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: To get rid of the need for pain relief

explanation: Active management uses medications to help the uterus clamp down fast, saving precious blood the mother cannot afford to lose.

question: What happens to a mother's body when her diet lacks proper nutrition during pregnancy?

options.A: Maternal blood volume increases beyond normal limits
options.B: The fetus draws nutrients from the mother's own body stores
options.C: Fetal growth remains completely unaffected by maternal diet
options.D: The placenta stops growing completely to save energy

explanation: When food intake is low, the clever baby takes what it needs from your own body reserves! This is why mums can feel so drained. You're doing great learning how the body adapts.

question: What is the most important immediate nursing action after a fasting blood draw for a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Provide food and allow the patient to take held morning medications.
options.B: Send the patient home immediately without checking the puncture site.
options.C: Instruct the patient to continue fasting until the lab results return.
options.D: Encourage the patient to run on a treadmill to lower blood sugar.

explanation: Well done! Because the patient fasted and held their morning diabetes drugs, they need food and their routine medications right away to prevent their blood sugar from crashing.

question: What does drug efficacy refer to?

options.A: The exact cost of the pharmaceutical item
options.B: The maximum response a drug can produce
options.C: The chemical stability of the drug bottle
options.D: The speed of absorption through the gut

explanation: Efficacy is the highest peak of relief or healing that a medication can possibly deliver for your patient.

question: Why is home health care such a big win for the Nigerian healthcare system?

options.A: It removes the need for trained nursing professionals
options.B: It helps decongest overcrowded tertiary hospitals
options.C: It guarantees uninterrupted electricity supply in every home
options.D: It completely eliminates the cost of medical supplies

explanation: True! Managing stable patients at home takes a huge load off our busy public hospitals.

question: A patient needs a low-sodium diet, but someone else cooks for their large family. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Instruct the family to hide all salt shakers inside the kitchen cabinets
options.B: Involve the family member who cooks in the dietary education sessions
options.C: Provide a strict list of forbidden foods with zero explanation
options.D: Advise the patient to cook separate meals only for themselves

explanation: Spot on! Since the family handles the cooking, bringing them into the teaching session ensures the patient actually gets the right meals at home.

question: Why is a patient told to take a deep breath and hold it while a chest or surgical drain is being removed?

options.A: It increases pressure and prevents air from entering the body cavity
options.B: It completely stops the patient from feeling any discomfort at all
options.C: It relaxes the abdominal muscles so the stitches fall apart
options.D: It forces the remaining fluid to rush out before the hole seals

explanation: Holding the breath creates a little bit of internal pressure, stopping air from being sucked into the empty tract as the tube comes out.

question: What is a very common cause of acute (short-term) fatigue?

options.A: A recent viral infection or short-term sleep loss
options.B: Long-standing, unmanaged hypothyroidism
options.C: Advanced autoimmune joint destruction
options.D: A multi-year history of clinical depression

explanation: Exactly! Acute fatigue usually pops up suddenly from something clear and temporary, like fighting off a cold or pulling a late-night reading session for exams.

question: How should a nurse handle someone who argues that there is 'no budget' for a new health project?

options.A: Ignore the stakeholder completely and proceed without their approval
options.B: Provide evidence showing financial losses caused by ignoring the issue
options.C: Offer to pay for the entire project out of the nurse's own salary
options.D: Argue loudly that the government is corrupt and does not care

explanation: Smart move! Showing them how much money the problem is *already* costing them helps turn a 'no budget' excuse into a reason to invest.

question: Who benefits the most when a community achieves herd immunity?

options.A: Patients recovering from surgical procedures
options.B: Only individuals with strong innate immunity
options.C: Vulnerable people who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: Only adults who travel to other countries

explanation: Spot on! Herd immunity builds a protective ring around fragile individuals who cannot take vaccines themselves.

question: What is the main job of a line diagram when looking at health data?

options.A: To display the exact percentage of blood types in a ward
options.B: To show data that changes continuously over time
options.C: To list the names of staff on duty during a shift
options.D: To compare different categories of unrelated patients

explanation: Spot on! Line diagrams are your go-to tool for connecting data points over days, weeks, or months to track trends easily.

question: What is the primary function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum inside a muscle fiber?

options.A: Anchoring the muscle to nearby bone tissue
options.B: Transmitting nerve impulses along the surface
options.C: Producing ATP through aerobic respiration
options.D: Storing and releasing calcium ions

explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum holds calcium ions until an electrical impulse triggers their release to start contraction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the main reason nurses use a genogram?

options.A: To prescribe strong mental health drugs to relatives
options.B: To map out family relationships and health patterns across generations
options.C: To calculate the household's exact monthly salary
options.D: To check the caregiver's blood pressure

explanation: A genogram is basically a detailed family tree that helps you spot inherited health issues and relationship patterns at a single glance.

question: At least how long must a diaphragm stay in after sex?

options.A: Twenty-four hours
options.B: One hour
options.C: Six hours
options.D: Twelve hours

explanation: Leaving it in for at least 6 hours gives the spermicide enough time to completely immobilize and destroy all viable sperm.

question: Why must a community health nurse pay attention to local values and cultural beliefs?

options.A: Beliefs dictate the exact amount of tax a patient must pay
options.B: Cultural norms influence how people perceive illness and treatment
options.C: Values determine whether a hospital bed is comfortable
options.D: Local customs replace the need for sterile medical equipment

explanation: Spot on! People view their symptoms and decide whether to accept treatment based on the cultural values they grew up with.

question: What is the typical clinical effect of a beta-blocker drug?

options.A: Stimulation of digestive motility and saliva production
options.B: Decreased heart rate and lowered blood pressure
options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels and pupils
options.D: Increased heart rate and dilated bronchial tubes

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline from working on the heart, helping it beat slower and with less force. This is great for managing high blood pressure!

question: What ethical dilemma frequently occurs during public health disease outbreaks?

options.A: Choosing which brand of uniform the nursing staff should wear
options.B: Deciding whether hospitals should serve hot or cold meals
options.C: Determining the exact cost of parking at the clinic gate
options.D: Balancing individual autonomy with community safety

explanation: Public health nurses often navigate the tension between personal freedom and protecting the wider public from contagious illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is the main goal of doing a Job Safety Analysis (JSA)?

options.A: Conducting routine blood pressure checks on factory workers
options.B: Calculating the monthly profit margin of an industrial plant
options.C: Breaking down a task step-by-step to spot hidden dangers
options.D: Measuring the exact decibel levels of factory machinery

explanation: A JSA looks at every little step of a job to catch safety risks before someone gets hurt. Teamwork makes safety work!

question: Why is it so important to include informal sector workers in Nigerian health insurance schemes?

options.A: It stops people from visiting traditional healers
options.B: It ensures that doctors no longer have to work in rural areas
options.C: It broadens the financial base and pools risk more effectively
options.D: It reduces the total population requiring medical care

explanation: Since a huge portion of Nigeria's workforce is in the informal sector, including them is the key to achieving true universal health coverage for everyone!

question: How much food should you put on the spoon when feeding an adult patient?

options.A: Just a single tiny drop
options.B: One-third to one-half full
options.C: Overflowing with extra gravy
options.D: Packed tightly to the very top

explanation: Smaller spoonfuls are much easier and safer for the patient to chew and swallow without getting overwhelmed.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier stopping women from using post-abortion contraception?

options.A: Fear of unpleasant side effects
options.B: Lack of transport to the clinic
options.C: Guaranteed 100 percent long-term effectiveness
options.D: High product costs at the pharmacy

explanation: High effectiveness is a great thing! Fear, cost, and travel issues are the real hurdles patients face.

question: When a yellow fever patient enters the dangerous intoxication phase, which organs take the hardest hit?

options.A: Skin and joints
options.B: Liver and kidneys
options.C: Lungs and brain
options.D: Heart and pancreas

explanation: Well done! This severe stage targets vital internal organs, especially the liver (causing the yellow eyes) and the kidneys. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h3)

question: What do second-order neurons typically do in ascending sensory pathways?

options.A: They secrete neurotransmitters onto sweat glands
options.B: They directly connect skin receptors to motor neurons
options.C: They cross the midline and ascend to the thalamus
options.D: They store long-term sensory memories in the frontal lobe

explanation: You got it! Second-order neurons cross over (decussate) to the opposite side of the spinal cord or brainstem before heading up to the thalamus.

question: Which lab test is the most reliable way to track declining kidney function?

options.A: Platelet aggregation rate
options.B: White blood cell count
options.C: Serum sodium concentration
options.D: Glomerular filtration rate

explanation: The GFR (Glomerular Filtration Rate) tells us directly how well the kidneys are cleaning the blood, making it the gold standard for checking kidney health.

question: What is a common myth used to justify FGM regarding hygiene?

options.A: Clipping the tissue improves daily personal hygiene efficiency
options.B: Uncut female genitalia are considered dirty and masculine
options.C: Surgical removal prevents all future skin infections
options.D: Natural anatomy causes unpleasant odors during adolescence

explanation: You got it! A widespread cultural myth falsely labels natural female anatomy as unclean.

question: Which type of medication is often given to calm down an overactive bladder?

options.A: Anticholinergics
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Anticoagulants
options.D: Diuretics

explanation: Anticholinergic drugs block the nerve signals that tell the bladder muscle to squeeze too often. It helps the bladder relax!

question: Why is it so important to find the root cause of a gap found during an audit?

options.A: To justify closing down the nursing department permanently
options.B: To make sure every single nurse on duty receives a formal warning
options.C: So the corrective action actually fixes the real underlying problem
options.D: To prove that the hospital administration has zero funds left

explanation: You nailed it! Finding the root cause ensures we fix the actual issue—whether it's a lack of training or a shortage of supplies—rather than just guessing.

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders right from the start of a health project?

options.A: It builds a sense of ownership and encourages community cooperation
options.B: It ensures that only the wealthiest families get treated
options.C: It stops the community from asking questions
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to do any work at all

explanation: When leaders feel involved from day one, they champion the project themselves, leading to wonderful community trust and success!

question: What is the standard dose of PPD administered during a Mantoux test?

options.A: 1.0 mL containing 50 tuberculin units
options.B: 0.1 mL containing 5 tuberculin units
options.C: 0.5 mL containing 10 tuberculin units
options.D: 2.0 mL containing 100 tuberculin units

explanation: The standard diagnostic dose for standard PPD screening is exactly 0.1 mL, which equals 5 tuberculin units. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why do we need to start CPR immediately when someone goes into cardiac arrest?

options.A: The lungs will collapse permanently within thirty seconds
options.B: Body temperature drops too fast for resuscitation to work
options.C: Brain damage begins within minutes due to lack of oxygen
options.D: Blood clots will instantly form in all major blood vessels

explanation: Spot on! When the heart stops, oxygen stops reaching the brain right away. Acting fast prevents permanent damage and saves lives.

question: Why is asking a patient about their recent travel and where they live so important during a nursing assessment?

options.A: It proves whether the patient paid their hospital registration bills
options.B: It determines the patient's exact health insurance coverage tier
options.C: It helps identify exposure to specific infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: It replaces the need for standard laboratory diagnostic tests

explanation: Great thinking! Knowing where a patient has been helps link their current symptoms to ongoing disease outbreaks in those areas.

question: Which method is best for reaching a large, scattered rural population across multiple villages at the same time?

options.A: A written textbook distributed to homes
options.B: Radio broadcast jingles
options.C: A silent demonstration with no sound
options.D: Individual bedside whispered counseling

explanation: Correct! Radio is a fantastic mass media tool to share quick health tips with people in areas you cannot visit every day.

question: What key engineering feature protects underground water sources underneath a proper sanitary landfill?

options.A: Open drainage ditches filled with gravel
options.B: Deep burning pits without concrete walls
options.C: Direct connection to municipal storm water pipes
options.D: Impermeable bottom liners and leachate collection systems

explanation: Special heavy-duty bottom liners and drainage pipes catch contaminated liquids (leachate) so they don't soak down into our drinking water table.

question: A patient agrees they are sick, stays home from classes, and asks family members if they look feverish. Which stage of illness is this?

options.A: Assumption of the sick role
options.B: Recovery and rehabilitation
options.C: Symptom experience
options.D: Dependent-patient role

explanation: When you step back from your daily duties and look for validation from loved ones that you need rest, you've entered the sick role.

question: When is the best time for a nurse to screen a patient for gender-based violence?

options.A: Only after the patient asks for police assistance
options.B: Exclusively during annual national health campaigns
options.C: Privately and routinely during clinical assessments
options.D: Loudly in a crowded waiting room for everyone to hear

explanation: Brilliant! Screening must always happen in a private, confidential space so the patient feels safe enough to open up to you.

question: What causes severe anemia in a patient with advanced malaria?

options.A: A complete failure of dietary iron absorption in the gut
options.B: Sudden internal bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Suppression of kidney function leading to blood loss in urine
options.D: Destruction and rapid loss of red blood cells by the parasite

explanation: Correct! As the malaria parasites multiply and break open red blood cells en masse, the patient's blood count drops sharply, causing severe anemia.

question: A hospital board decides to build three new community health centers over the next four years. What type of objective does this represent?

options.A: Strategic objective
options.B: Individual performance objective
options.C: Daily shift objective
options.D: Operational objective

explanation: Long-term, multi-year plans involving major resource commitments are classic examples of strategic objectives. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h3)

question: What does 'test-retest reliability' check in a study?

options.A: Stability of scores over time
options.B: Agreement between two different observers
options.C: Equivalence of two different questionnaire versions
options.D: Internal similarity of survey questions

explanation: Spot on! Test-retest simply means giving the same test to the same people at two different times to see if the scores stay stable.

question: A patient with Addison's disease gets a severe stomach infection and comes to the ER very weak, confused, and with dangerously low blood pressure. What is happening?

options.A: Cushing's syndrome
options.B: Addisonian crisis
options.C: Pheochromocytoma storm
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: This is an emergency! When a physical stressor like an infection hits someone with Addison's, their body can crash into an Addisonian crisis due to a sudden lack of cortisol. Quick fluids and steroids save lives here.

question: Where are cytochrome P450 enzymes mostly found in the human body?

options.A: In the kidneys
options.B: In the liver
options.C: In the bone marrow
options.D: In the skeletal muscles

explanation: You nailed it! The liver is packed with cytochrome P450 enzymes, making it the main engine for breaking down drugs in our bodies. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h3)

question: When lifestyle changes don't quite cut it, what type of medication is usually recommended first for pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Heavy narcotic pain relievers
options.B: Prescription laxatives
options.C: Strong proton pump inhibitors
options.D: Antacids containing calcium or magnesium

explanation: Calcium and magnesium antacids work fast to neutralize acid and have a safe track record during pregnancy.

question: A patient stays completely quiet during a health talk. What is a common mistake nurses make when interpreting this?

options.A: Assuming it means full agreement when it may reflect quiet distress
options.B: Documenting that the client has a severe hearing impairment
options.C: Reporting the client immediately to the hospital ethics board
options.D: Stopping all medications until the client speaks out loud

explanation: Be careful here! In many of our local cultures, quietness out of respect doesn't mean they actually agree or even understand. Always gently check in!

question: How did the primary health care approach fundamentally change the traditional focus of medicine?

options.A: It transferred all health funding directly to private pharmaceutical companies
options.B: It shifted the focus from hospital treatment to community prevention
options.C: It made advanced surgical procedures free for all citizens
options.D: It replaced traditional healers with foreign medical doctors

explanation: Primary health care moved medicine away from expensive curative hospital care toward keeping communities healthy through prevention. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: In patients with high blood pressure, what common recovery factor can trigger a dangerous blood pressure spike?

options.A: Pain and anxiety
options.B: Sleeping on the left side
options.C: Eating fresh vegetables
options.D: Drinking too much water

explanation: When a patient feels pain or emotional stress, their nervous system kicks in, which can cause their blood pressure to shoot up.

question: What practical change can nurses advocate for to help more men attend clinics?

options.A: Charging male visitors a special facility fee
options.B: Scheduling weekend or evening clinic hours
options.C: Requiring fathers to wear special uniforms
options.D: Banning all female relatives from the waiting room

explanation: Flexible clinic hours make it possible for men who work during regular weekdays to attend.

question: Why is feeling things through your skin so important for everyday survival?

options.A: It provides the primary energy source for epidermal cells.
options.B: It alerts the body to immediate physical dangers in the environment.
options.C: It prevents the accumulation of lactic acid in muscle tissue.
options.D: It controls the hormonal output of the pituitary gland.

explanation: Spot on! Being able to feel pain or extreme heat and cold lets your body react in a flash to avoid serious injury.

question: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of which common virus is the primary cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Epstein-Barr Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: High-risk types of HPV can cause gradual changes in the cells of the cervix. Over time, these changes can turn cancerous if not caught early by a Pap smear.

question: A pregnant mum taking daily iron pills complains of severe constipation. What is the main reason behind this?

options.A: Iron vitamins cause the stomach to shrink in size
options.B: Iron instantly stops the production of all digestive juices
options.C: Excess iron unabsorbed in the gut binds and hardens the stool
options.D: Iron forces the body to expel water through the skin instead

explanation: Well thought out! The iron that the body doesn't absorb interacts inside the gut, turning the waste firmer and harder to pass.

question: What is the main physical outcome of body scarification?

options.A: Rapidly fading surface cuts
options.B: Deep muscle tissue damage
options.C: Permanent scars on the skin
options.D: Temporary skin discoloration

explanation: Scarification is designed to leave lasting, textured marks on the skin that stay with a person for life. Great job keeping this fundamental concept in mind!

question: A patient can no longer feel hot or cold water on their foot after a back injury. Which pathway is likely affected?

options.A: Corticospinal tract
options.B: Spinothalamic tract
options.C: Cauda equina
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: You got this! The spinothalamic pathway is our body's dedicated highway for carrying pain, temperature, and touch sensations up to the brain.

question: What is a normal, healthy reason for a small amount of fluid to appear in the Pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Uterine fibroid growth
options.B: Recent ovulation
options.C: Cervical dilation
options.D: Endometrial shedding

explanation: Brilliant! When an egg is released during ovulation, a tiny, totally harmless amount of fluid escapes and pools in the pelvis. Totally normal!

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to care for skin receiving radiation therapy?

options.A: Scrub the treatment area firmly with a washcloth daily
options.B: Use heating pads on the skin to relieve soreness
options.C: Wash the area gently with mild soap and warm water
options.D: Apply strong perfumed lotions right before treatment

explanation: Treated skin is extra fragile. Gentle cleansing with mild soap and water protects the delicate skin barrier. You're mastering patient care!

question: Which of these medications would you NOT give directly into the heart muscle for routine pain relief?

options.A: Calcium chloride
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Morphine sulfate
options.D: Atropine

explanation: Morphine is a pain reliever (analgesic), not a cardiac arrest drug. It is never poked straight into the heart muscle!

question: What is a primary responsibility of the nurse when initiating a referral?

options.A: Transporting the client personally in her private vehicle
options.B: Performing major surgeries before sending the client away
options.C: Preparing the client emotionally and explaining the reason for referral
options.D: Purchasing the client's transport fare out of her own pocket

explanation: Nurses must counsel clients so they understand why a referral is necessary and feel less anxious about visiting a new facility. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h6)

question: Why does a teenage boy's voice crack and deepen?

options.A: Hypertrophy of the salivary glands from increased testosterone
options.B: Narrowing of the pharynx due to rapid facial bone growth
options.C: Elongation of the vocal cords due to laryngeal cartilage growth
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by an upper respiratory infection

explanation: Well done! Testosterone makes the voice box (larynx) grow larger, stretching the vocal cords and dropping the pitch of the voice.

question: How often should a patient who sits in a wheelchair perform weight shifts to prevent skin breakdown?

options.A: Only when their skin starts to turn red
options.B: Every fifteen to thirty minutes
options.C: Once a day right before bedtime
options.D: Once every four to six hours

explanation: Frequent short weight shifts relieve pressure long enough for blood to circulate back into the compressed skin tissues. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why is prevalence data most useful for community health nurses?

options.A: It proves the exact day a patient contracted an illness
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical diagnosis in the field
options.C: It stops new infections from entering the community
options.D: It helps plan long-term care and allocate resources

explanation: Knowing the total burden of disease helps nurses and health planners prepare adequate facilities and supplies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is just counting calories often not enough when caring for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Calories change drastically depending on the time of day a meal is served
options.B: Calories do not reflect whether the body can actually absorb and use the nutrients
options.C: Patient metabolism makes calorie tracking completely impossible in a hospital
options.D: Processed foods always have lower calorie counts than raw food items

explanation: Great thinking! A meal can be packed with calories yet lack the vital building blocks our cells and tissues need to heal.

question: Why is it risky to ignore signs of depression in a patient managing a blood disorder?

options.A: Depression automatically causes an immediate drop in haemoglobin levels
options.B: Patients with depression are legally barred from receiving blood transfusions
options.C: Sadness always leads to permanent physical paralysis if left unmanaged
options.D: Untreated depression can severely reduce treatment adherence and self-care

explanation: When patients feel hopeless, they might skip clinic visits or meds. Spotting depression early keeps them on track with their healing.

question: A patient with heart failure suddenly feels short of breath. Which nursing action should you take first regarding their position?

options.A: Place the patient face down in the prone position
options.B: Elevate the head of the bed to semi-Fowler's
options.C: Tilt the bed head downward into Trendelenburg
options.D: Lay the patient completely flat in the supine position

explanation: Sitting them up in semi-Fowler's makes breathing so much easier by taking pressure off their lungs and heart. Great job!

question: Which macronutrient requires the most energy for the body to digest and process?

options.A: Refined oil
options.B: Protein
options.C: Simple sugar
options.D: Dietary fat

explanation: Protein has a high thermic effect, forcing the body to expend more calories during its breakdown and metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h5)

question: When should you as a nurse switch to surgical asepsis instead of medical asepsis?

options.A: Before giving oral medication to a patient in the general ward
options.B: During any procedure that enters a normally sterile body cavity
options.C: After finishing a routine bed bath for an adult patient
options.D: Whenever entering a patient room with a known respiratory infection

explanation: You're doing great! Whenever we do invasive things like passing a catheter or assisting in theater, we need total sterility to protect deep body tissues from infection.

question: What is the main way the heart automatically matches its blood supply to its workload?

options.A: Opening of heart valves during systole
options.B: Control by the kidneys via blood pressure
options.C: Local metabolic autoregulation
options.D: Direct command from the cerebral cortex

explanation: Correct! The heart uses smart local chemical changes in its own tissue to automatically adjust vessel size and keep the blood flowing where it's needed most.

question: A patient with severe rheumatoid arthritis has painful, swollen finger joints. Which property of NSAIDs makes them so helpful here?

options.A: Anti-inflammatory action
options.B: Bronchodilator action
options.C: Antibiotic action
options.D: Sedative action

explanation: Since rheumatoid arthritis involves angry, swollen joints, the anti-inflammatory power of NSAIDs helps calm that immune response right down. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is long-term (chronic) stress tougher on the body than short-term stress?

options.A: It causes immediate physical injury like broken bones
options.B: It lingers over a long period and wears down body defenses
options.C: It only affects people living in rural agricultural areas
options.D: It completely stops the heart within a few seconds

explanation: While a quick burst of stress can help you run from danger, staying stressed for months wears your body down and opens the door to sickness.

question: When does the assessment of a patient's mental status actually begin?

options.A: Only after the deep tendon reflexes are completed
options.B: The moment you first greet and observe the patient
options.C: After the patient falls asleep for the night
options.D: When the laboratory blood work results return

explanation: Observation of appearance, alertness, and interaction starts immediately upon entering the room. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is one of the biggest threats to the long-term success of mobile healthcare outreach programs?

options.A: Strict government regulations prohibiting community-level nursing practice
options.B: A complete lack of interest from community members in receiving care
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced diagnostic machinery in rural villages
options.D: Difficulty in sustaining funding and services after initial project phases end

explanation: Many great programs struggle when initial donor funds or temporary support run dry. It's a major challenge in community nursing!

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: To check the outer muscles that move the eyeball around
options.B: To view the internal structures of the back of the eye
options.C: To test the patient for clear distance and reading vision
options.D: To measure the exact fluid pressure inside the eyeball

explanation: Ophthalmoscopy specifically directs light through the pupil to examine the internal fundus, which includes the retina and optic disc. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h1)

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar result comes back at 115 mg/dL. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: It is completely normal and requires no further follow-up.
options.B: It indicates prediabetes or impaired fasting glucose.
options.C: It confirms that the patient has full-blown Type 1 diabetes.
options.D: It shows severe hypoglycemia requiring immediate sugar intake.

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL fall into the prediabetes range, signaling a need for lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h6)

question: How do certain bacteria and fungi manage to survive harsh sun and dry air up in the atmosphere?

options.A: They grow wings to fly away from sunny areas
options.B: They absorb all the pollution particles to feed themselves
options.C: They immediately transform into non-living chemical gases
options.D: They produce protective structures like spores or thick outer coats

explanation: Correct! Spores and tough coats act like a shield, keeping microbes safe until they land somewhere nice.

question: What is the main goal of giving ovulation-stimulating medications like clomiphene citrate?

options.A: To thicken the uterine lining permanently
options.B: To clear blocked fallopian tubes
options.C: To increase male testosterone levels
options.D: To encourage the release of mature eggs

explanation: These helpful drugs nudge the ovaries to develop and release eggs when a woman's ovulation is irregular.

question: Which genetic change is most often linked to primary polycythaemia vera?

options.A: JAK2 mutation
options.B: BRCA1 mutation
options.C: CFTR mutation
options.D: Factor V Leiden

explanation: A mutation in the JAK2 gene is the classic signature of primary polycythaemia vera. It tells the bone marrow to keep dividing cells non-stop.

question: Which part of the brain is responsible for releasing Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)?

options.A: The hypothalamus
options.B: The cerebral cortex
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: You got it! The hypothalamus acts as the master control center in the brain, pulsing out GnRH to kickstart reproductive development.

question: You are getting ready to give IV phenytoin to a patient. Which IV fluid should you use to flush and dilute it?

options.A: 5% Dextrose in Normal Saline
options.B: Sterile distilled water
options.C: 5% Dextrose in Water
options.D: 0.9% Normal Saline

explanation: Phenytoin hates sugar! If you mix it with any IV fluid containing dextrose, it will clump up and form crystals right in the tubing. Always stick to normal saline.

question: What is the VERY FIRST thing a nurse must do if a patient shows signs of a transfusion reaction?

options.A: Call the hospital maintenance team
options.B: Administer an oral pain reliever
options.C: Slow down the infusion pump rate
options.D: Stop the transfusion immediately

explanation: Safety first! Stopping the flow immediately keeps any more of the incompatible blood from entering their body. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: A patient with a head injury starts acting impulsively and makes poor daily choices. Which lobe is most likely affected?

options.A: Parietal lobe
options.B: Temporal lobe
options.C: Occipital lobe
options.D: Frontal lobe

explanation: The prefrontal portion of the frontal lobe governs reasoning, impulse control, and executive decision-making. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h2)

question: Which nutrient-rich foods are very often forbidden to pregnant women in many traditional settings?

options.A: Cassava flakes
options.B: Hard white yam
options.C: Refined table salt
options.D: Eggs and meat

question: Why is it unsafe to leave frozen meat sitting on a warm kitchen counter to thaw?

options.A: It causes the meat to lose all of its nutritional value
options.B: It freezes the center of the meat even harder
options.C: Surface bacteria multiply rapidly as the outer layers warm up
options.D: It turns the meat into a poisonous chemical substance

explanation: Makes total sense, right? As the outer layers warm up to room temperature, they enter the 'danger zone' where bacteria throw a party and multiply fast.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a specific phobia?

options.A: Fear of heights
options.B: Fear of social judgment
options.C: Fear of leaving the house
options.D: Fear of public speaking

explanation: Fear of heights (acrophobia) is a classic specific phobia tied to a distinct environmental trigger. Simple and straightforward!

question: A patient with a wound infected by a multi-drug resistant organism needs which type of precaution?

options.A: Respiratory isolation
options.B: Protective isolation
options.C: Contact isolation
options.D: Airborne isolation

explanation: Resistant germs in open wounds are typically passed through physical touch, making contact isolation necessary. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: In the famous ABCDE emergency checklist, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Behavior
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Breathing
options.D: Bedside

question: Why is avoiding a fever important for a patient recovering from cardiac arrest?

options.A: Fever stops the heart from responding to standard medications
options.B: Fever increases the brain's need for oxygen and worsens injury
options.C: Fever causes the intravenous lines to clot off quickly
options.D: Fever makes it impossible to check the patient's blood pressure

question: What is the golden rule for someone receiving a delegated task (the delegatee)?

options.A: To independently change the patient care plan if complications arise
options.B: To accept only tasks within their training and scope of practice
options.C: To take over full legal liability for the entire ward
options.D: To perform advanced clinical assessments on unstable patients

explanation: Safety first! A delegatee should only ever take on tasks they have been properly trained and authorized to perform.

question: Why is regular mouth care with antiseptic solution so important for a patient on a ventilator?

options.A: To stimulate saliva production for better digestion
options.B: To check if the patient has a gag reflex
options.C: To reduce bacterial buildup that can lead to lung infections
options.D: To prevent the endotracheal tube from sticking to the lips

question: Which statistical test do researchers commonly use to check internal consistency?

options.A: Chi-square test
options.B: Student's t-test
options.C: Pearson correlation
options.D: Cronbach's alpha

question: A patient is officially diagnosed with AIDS when their CD4 count drops below which threshold?

question: You are serving lunch to a patient who is legally blind. What is the best way to help them eat independently?

options.B: Feed the patient spoonful by spoonful to save time
options.C: Mix all the food together so it is easier to scoop up
options.D: Describe the layout of the food using the clock-face method

question: A patient having a severe asthma attack gets an intravenous steroid. What is the main goal of giving this in an emergency?

options.A: To thin out thick mucus plugs blocking the lower lung passages

options.C: To boost the patient's heart rate and increase oxygen delivery

question: Which of these is a direct legal duty for a nurse administrator?

question: What is the main feature of quantitative data collection?

options.A: They rely entirely on the researcher's personal feelings and intuition
options.B: They avoid using any structured tools or standardized checklists
options.C: They produce numerical data that can be measured and analyzed statistically
options.D: They focus exclusively on recording long, emotional personal stories

question: How do dendrites differ in function from axons?

options.A: Dendrites are found only in the brain, while axons are in the spinal cord

options.D: Dendrites control voluntary movement, while axons control involuntary actions
